column1: # Per-machine timing baselines — DESIGN.md §6, ADR-0016.
# Tab-separated. Columns:
#   cpu       the CPU model, in the exact spelling `scripts/check-machine.sh`
#             prints and `harness.rs` reads back. STATUS.md open item 20 measured
#             that this is the key that works: two EPYC generations in one CI
#             pool differ 21% on `ring, one way` while either one holds to ~1%.
#   case      the case name passed to `Suite::bench`, exactly.
#   baseline  ns/op, the MEDIAN over `n` whole runs of the suite. Not one run:
#             the same box gives 267.2-335.7 for `ring, one way`.
#   margin    what this case is allowed to drift on THIS machine before it counts
#             as a regression. Smallest step of 1.10 / 1.15 / 1.20 / 1.25 / 1.30 /
#             1.35 that is >= the max/median measured over those `n` runs; 1.10 is
#             the floor. A margin off that ladder, or changed without a new `n`
#             and date beside it, is a hand-nudge and shows up as one in the diff.
#   n         how many whole suite runs the two numbers above came from.
#   date      when.
#   verdict   what `scripts/check-machine.sh` said for that run. A line whose
#             verdict is not `pass 10 fail 0` is NOT a publishable latency figure
#             — CLAUDE.md §2 non-negotiable 10 — and DESIGN.md §6 marks it so.
# To add a machine: run `scripts/bench.sh` until check-machine.sh reads
# `pass 10 fail 0`, then N >= 20 more times, and paste the medians. The harness
# prints a paste-ready line for every case it has no baseline for.
# Measure through `scripts/bench.sh`, not through the bench targets directly.
# `[measured 2026-08-31]` a baseline taken by running the four timing targets on
# their own put `encode ExecutionReport` over its limit on the first bench.sh run
# it met: bench.sh runs eight targets and the case is not measured in the same
# state. Leave a gap between runs, too -- back-to-back, the previous suite is
# still inside check-machine.sh's one-second window and the run reads 25-36% busy
# and disqualifies itself.
# The margin covers the widest excursion seen in ANY qualifying run on this
# machine, not just the sample the median came from. `ring, one way` never drew
# its second mode across these 24 runs, but earlier samples reached 336.3 ns; a
# margin fitted to this sample alone would sit below that and go red on a mode
# that is known, documented and not a regression.
# One deliberate exclusion, stated so it is not silent: `inline deliver + reply`
# read 6.3-8.3 ns under the PREVIOUS harness, and those runs are not counted
# towards its margin. `[measured 2026-08-31]` about 5 of those 6.3 ns were the
# harness itself -- the instrument was replaced, so its readings describe an
# apparatus that no longer exists. Every other case is within 1% across the two
# harnesses and needs no such judgement.
# Three cases carry a margin wider than the 1.10 floor, and it is not slop:
# `[measured 2026-08-31]` they are bimodal or trimodal PER PROCESS, so the
# harness's best-of-7 samples all land inside whichever mode that process drew.
# See docs/reference/measured-costs.md.
